events.title: Webpack 5 released
events.summary: Webpack 5.0 shipped on October 10, 2020 with persistent caching, module federation, and improved tree-shaking.
events.about: Webpack 5's module federation let micro-frontends share dependencies at runtime — a pattern adopted by large enterprises. Persistent caching sped CI builds; better tree-shaking reduced bundle sizes for [React] and Vue apps still on webpack before [Vite]'s rise.

narrative.whyChosen: Webpack 5 module federation changed how teams composed large frontends.
narrative.whyImportant: Runtime sharing of modules enabled independent deployable micro-frontends.
narrative.problemSolved: Monolithic frontends could not be split into independently deployed apps without duplicate bundles.

events.title: Google Pixel 5 released
events.summary: Google began selling the Google [Pixel] 5 — mid-range pivot with wireless charging in aluminum body.
events.about: [Nexus] and [Pixel] phones were Google's pure-[Android] reference hardware for developers. Mid-range pivot with wireless charging in aluminum body. [AOSP] builds and CTS testing often used [Pixel] devices as the baseline.

narrative.whyChosen: The Google [Pixel] 5 was a flagship Google [Android] reference device.
narrative.whyImportant: [Pixel]/[Nexus] hardware defines the reference [Android] experience for developers.
narrative.problemSolved: [Android] needed first-party reference phones without [OEM] skin fragmentation.

events.title: iPhone 12 released
events.summary: Apple began selling the iPhone 12 on October 23, 2020 — 5G, flat-edge design, and MagSafe accessories.
events.about: 5G connectivity changed how developers thought about mobile bandwidth; MagSafe created a new accessory and charging [API] ecosystem. The flat design returned to a form factor reminiscent of iPhone 4/5 industrial design.

narrative.whyChosen: The iPhone 12 brought 5G and MagSafe to the mainstream iPhone line.
narrative.whyImportant: 5G and magnetic accessory attachment opened new mobile hardware interaction patterns.
narrative.problemSolved: iPhones lacked 5G radios; wireless charging alignment was finicky without magnets.

events.title: Starlink opens public beta
events.summary: SpaceX invited early subscribers to its "Better Than Nothing Beta" on October 26, 2020 — the first public consumer satellite broadband service using a LEO constellation.
events.about: Starlink ships a user terminal and Wi-Fi router that talks to hundreds of low-Earth-orbit satellites — targeting rural and mobile users where fiber and LTE are weak. Developers testing offline-tolerant apps, high-latency links, and global field deployments gained a new real-world network profile beyond terrestrial ISPs.

narrative.whyChosen: Starlink's public beta made consumer satellite internet a shipping product, not a defense-only niche.
narrative.whyImportant: It added a third access architecture (LEO satellite) beside cable, DSL, and terrestrial cellular.
narrative.problemSolved: Rural homes and mobile workers lacked affordable broadband with usable latency for modern web apps.
